title: Bluetooth 5 (BLE) link-layer peripheral on a 1 bit per clock baseband: ADV_IND from a host payload, SCAN_REQ / SCAN_RSP, CONNECT_REQ, connection events with SN / NESN acknowledgement, peripheral latency and supervision timeout

words.name: ADV_CTRL
words.desc: bit 0 adv_en: send ADV_IND every ADV_INTV clocks while advertising (write only; reset 1)

words.name: SCAN_CTRL
words.desc: bit 0 scan_en: answer SCAN_REQ with SCAN_RSP (write only; reset 1)

regs.name: STATUS
regs.desc: Baseband state, as driven on the pin

fields.desc: high while a packet is being sent on txd

irqs.name: ERROR
irqs.desc: a bad CRC24, an unknown advertising PDU type, a reserved LLID, a length above 16, a CONNECT_REQ of the wrong length, or a supervision timeout (back to advertising)

notes: rxd and txd are the baseband pins (1 bit per PCLK, LSB first); they pass through unchanged. tx_act also drives a pin.

The core's configuration port has no read side, so PAY0..PAY15, ADV_CTRL and SCAN_CTRL are write only and read as 0. A write must set all four byte strobes (the low 8 bits are used); a partial-strobe write gets PSLVERR and is dropped. The payload is read while ADV_IND is sent, so a write during a packet can change it mid-way.
Simplified link layer (see rtl/Bluetooth5_top.sv): advertising channel 37 only, the 15-byte CONNECT_REQ, channel selection algorithm #1 without a channel map.
